title: 2016 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement: All three vertices of \(\bigtriangleup ABC\) lie on the parabola defined by \(y=x^2,\) with \(A\) at the origin and \(\overline{BC}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis. The area of the triangle is \(64.\) What is the length of \(BC?\)

solutions.text:
Let the points be \[A=(0,0),\]\[B=(x_1,y_1),\]\[C=(x_2,y_2).\]

Then, since \(BC\) is parallel with the \(x\)-axis, we know \(y_1=y_2,\) which we will let be \(y.\) Then, \(x_1^2 = y=x_2^2,\) so \(x_1^2=x_2^2 .\) This implies that either \(x_1=-x_2 \) or \(x_1 = x_2.\) The second option cannot happen since that would set two points as the same, which would create an area of \(0.\) As such, let \(x= -x_1=x_2.\) Then \(y=x^2\) also.

Then, the points are \[A=(0,0),\]\[B=(-x,x^2),\]\[C=(x,x^2).\] With a base of \(BC,\) the length is \(2x\) and the height is \(x^2.\) This would make the area \(x^3 = 64.\) Therefore, \(x=4,\) so \(BC = 2\cdot 4 = 8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C .
